newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's Aubry lost finance battle in new cabinet.
newsitem.headline: France's Aubry lost finance battle in new cabinet.

text.p: France's Martine Aubry, heading a superministry to fight unemployment, lost a battle in the forming of the Socialist-led cabinet when control over spending was awarded to the finance ministry, Socialist sources said on Friday.
New Economy, Finance and Industry Minister Dominique Strauss-Kahn will control the purse strings for Aubry's Ministry of Employment and Social Security in the cabinet formed on Wednesday.
The two strongly pro-European ministers will have to cooperate closely in spearheading a fight against France's record 12.8 percent unemployment in Prime Minister Lionel Jospin's government.

The daily Liberation said Aubry had been prepared to refuse a post in the government rather than accept one that did not satisfy her. For several hours on Monday night, she was leaning towards taking the justice ministry.

Aubry won concessions including the creation of a committee comprising Jospin, Aubry, Strauss-Kahn and Christian Sautter, secretary of state for the budget, to harmonise work and a certain right to oversee social security accounts.

Both Aubry, the daughter of former European Commission president Jacques Delors, and Strauss-Kahn favour the single European currency. Jospin has said he will not step up budget austerity to qualify for the euro.

Aubry is in charge of Jospin's target of creating 700,000 youth jobs and cutting the working week to 35 hours from 39 with no loss of pay -- and will have to square them with Socialist pledges not to raise taxes.
The daily Le Parisien also said Delors had dreamt of becoming foreign minister -- a post awarded to Hubert Vedrine, a former chief aide to the late president Francois Mitterrand.
It said that Jospin offered Delors the post of justice minister to use his spotless reputation in a country racked by political sleaze scandals. Delors refused.
